rules.prepare:
# As in Debian's rules. cd "$AELTRA_SOURCE_DIR" AM_OPTS=--copy LT_OPTS=--copy ./autogen.sh
# As in Alpine: musl only has stubs for the functions of utmpx.h, the # programs that record or show who is logged in use utmps there (agetty, # wall, lslogins, su, runuser; login leaves it to PAM with Debian's # patches). The flags put utmpx.h of utmps in front of the one of the C # library. Alpine links the library statically, here the shared one is # used. if [ "$AELTRA_LIBC_NAME" = "musl" ]; then UTMPS_CFLAGS="$("${AELTRA_HOST_TYPE}-pkg-config" --cflags libutmps)" UTMPS_LIBS="$("${AELTRA_HOST_TYPE}-pkg-config" --libs libutmps)"
export CFLAGS="${CFLAGS:--g -O2} $UTMPS_CFLAGS" export LDFLAGS="$LDFLAGS $UTMPS_LIBS" fi
# With the prefix /usr configure puts programs into /bin and /sbin and # libraries into /lib unless it is told where they go. On Aeltra these are # links to the folders below /usr, and that is where packages install. # # The options of Debian's rules, with these differences: no systemd, no # udev and no cryptsetup, which are not there, and at the end the options # that Debian does not have (no NLS, no bash completion, and the makefile # installs nothing setuid: the package files set those permissions). cd "$AELTRA_BUILD_DIR" $AELTRA_SOURCE_DIR/configure \ --prefix="$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX" \ --bindir="$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX/bin" \ --sbindir="$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX/sbin" \ --libdir="$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX/lib" \ --build="$AELTRA_HOST_TYPE" \ --host="$AELTRA_HOST_TYPE" \ --enable-usrdir-path \ --with-ntfs-mounttype=ntfs \ --disable-makeinstall-chown \ --with-selinux \ --with-smack \ --enable-partx \ --without-systemd \ --without-udev \ --with-audit \ --without-cryptsetup \ --enable-newgrp \ --enable-login \ --enable-nologin \ --disable-mesg \ --disable-write \ --without-python \ --disable-kill \ --disable-chfn-chsh \ --disable-cal \ --disable-last \ --disable-utmpdump \ --disable-hwclock-gplv3 \ --disable-nls \ --disable-bash-completion \ --disable-makeinstall-setuid
# During the first phase of package builds during bootstrapping, the build # system finds /tools/include/ncurses and adds /tools/include to the header # search path even when the prefix has been set to /usr. To work around that # we fix up all files with /tools/include inside before running the build.
if [ "$AELTRA_BUILD_FOR" = "target" ] && [ -d /tools/include/ncurses ]; then sed -i "s@/tools/include@/usr/include@g" $( grep -r -l -F "/tools/include" * | sort -u ) fi
rules.build:
if [ "$AELTRA_BUILD_FOR" = "tools" ]; then export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$AELTRA_BUILD_DIR/.libs" fi
cd "$AELTRA_BUILD_DIR" make -j"$AELTRA_PARALLEL_JOBS"
rules.install:
cd "$AELTRA_BUILD_DIR" make DESTDIR="$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR" install
cd "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX"
# As in Debian: no libtool files, and no static libraries but libuuid and # libblkid. rm -f lib/*.la lib/security/*.la rm -f lib/libfdisk.a lib/liblastlog2.a lib/libmount.a lib/libsmartcols.a
# As in Debian, these are in the program folder of users, who don't have # sbin in their path. Debian moves pivot_root and switch_root too. They # stay in sbin, where busybox has its links for these two names: in bin # they would not replace the applets but be there next to them. Otherwise # the programs are where upstream has them and are called what upstream # calls them, as in Alpine (Debian: rename.ul, the links getty, hd, sg). for PROG in addpart blkzone chcpu delpart ldattach partx resizepart; do mv "sbin/$PROG" bin/ done
# su, mount, umount and newgrp are setuid root. The package files say so # (mode="4755").
# Debian's PAM files, see package.xml. install -d -m 0755 "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/etc/pam.d" share/pam-configs for NAME in login remote; do case "$NAME" in login) SRC="login.pam" ;; *) SRC="login.$NAME.pam" ;; esac install -m 644 "$AELTRA_WORK_DIR/extra/$SRC" \ "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/etc/pam.d/$NAME" done for NAME in runuser runuser-l su su-l; do install -m 644 "$AELTRA_WORK_DIR/extra/util-linux.$NAME.pam" \ "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/etc/pam.d/$NAME" done install -m 644 "$AELTRA_WORK_DIR/extra/pam-configs/lastlog2" \ share/pam-configs/
